unit1_text: UNIT 1: INTRODUCTION TO MINE LEGISLATION & REGULATORY FRAMEWORK Historical Evolution of Mine Legislation in India: Pre-independence regulations, post-independence acts, international influences (e.g. ILO conventions).  Constitutional Provisions Related to Mines: Entry 54 of Union List, State List, Concurrent List – powers of Central and State Governments. The Mines Act, 1952: Objectives and scope of the Act, Definitions of key terms (mine, owner, agent, manager, competent person, serious bodily injury, etc.), Provisions related to health, safety, and welfare of workers, Employment of women and young persons, Notifiable diseases and accidents, Duties and responsibilities of owners, agents, and managers, Penalties for contravention. The Mines Rules, 1955: General provisions related to health and sanitation (drinking water, latrines, first aid), Provisions related to medical examination and certificates, Duties of workmen. Introduction to Key Regulatory Bodies: Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS) – historical background, organizational structure, powers, and functions.
unit2_text: UNIT 2: MINE SAFETY MANAGEMENT & HAZARDS IN MINES Principles of Mine Safety Management: Safety policy, safety organization, safety audit, safety management plan (SMP). Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) in Mines: Techniques and methodologies for identifying hazards, assessing risks, and implementing control measures. Major Hazards in Underground Mines: Ground Control: Roof falls, side falls, rock bursts, strata movement. Causes, prevention, and support systems, Explosions: Methane explosions, coal dust explosions. Causes, prevention (ventilation, stone dust barriers, explosion-proof equipment), and rescue, Fires: Spontaneous combustion, electrical fires. Causes, detection, prevention, and firefighting techniques, Inundation: Water inflow into mines. Causes, prevention, dewatering methods, Suffocation & Toxic Gases: Carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, hydrogen sulphide, oxides of nitrogen. Sources, detection, and control. Major Hazards in Opencast Mines: Slope Stability: Highwall and dump stability issues. Causes and remedial measures, Haulage and Transport Accidents: Dumpers, shovels, excavators. Causes, safe operating procedures, traffic management, Blasting Hazards: Flyrock, ground vibrations, air blast. Safe blasting practices, Dust & Noise Pollution: Health effects, control measures.
unit3_text: UNIT 3: MACHINERY SAFETY & ELECTRICAL SAFETY IN MINES Safety Features of Mining Machinery: Design considerations for safety, interlocks, emergency stops, guarding. Safe Operation and Maintenance of Mining Equipment: Shovels, excavators, dumpers, drills, loaders, conveyors, winders. Wire Ropes: Types, construction, inspection, maintenance, and testing. Haulage and Winding Systems Safety: Ropes, cages, skips, winding engines. Statutory provisions for winding. General Electrical Safety in Mines: Definitions (e.g. intrinsic safety, flameproof enclosure). Earthing practices, Protection against overcurrent, short circuit, and earth leakage, Insulation and cabling. Statutory Provisions for Electrical Installations: The Electricity Act, 2003 (relevant sections) and the Central Electricity Authority (Measures Relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations, 2010 (relevant to mines). Maintenance of Electrical Equipment: Inspection, testing, and record-keeping. Accident Investigation of Electrical Incidents.
unit4_text: UNIT 4: ACCIDENT PREVENTION, INVESTIGATION & EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS Accident Causation Theories: Domino theory, human error, Heinrich's triangle. Accident Prevention Techniques: Safety training and education, safety campaigns, personal protective equipment (PPE) – selection, use, and maintenance. Accident Reporting and Investigation: Statutory requirements for reporting accidents, Principles of accident investigation: data collection, root cause analysis, recommendations, Role of DGMS in accident investigation. Emergency Preparedness and Response: Mine emergency plans, Mine rescue services: Organization, equipment (self-rescuers, breathing apparatus), training, Firefighting and explosion control strategies, Inundation rescue and recovery, First aid and medical facilities in mines. Occupational Health & Hygiene in Mines: Common occupational diseases (pneumoconiosis, silicosis, noise-induced hearing loss), Prevention and control measures, Health surveillance. Role of Trade Unions and Workers' Participation in Safety. Recent Amendments and Future Trends in Mine Safety Legislation.

unit1_text: [07 Hours] Power Generation & Transmission in Mines Mechanical Power Transmission: belt drives, chain drives and gear drives; couplings (rigid, flexible, fluid); clutches and brakes used in mining machinery; basic selection criteria for mining duty. unit2_text: [08 Hours] Wire Ropes & Haulage Systems Wire Ropes: applications in surface and underground mines; construction, lays, classification (round-strand, locked-coil, non-stranded, flattened-strand); factor of safety; examination, testing, care and maintenance; capping (white-metal and resin) and splicing; rope capels; rope-changing procedure. Track Haulage: direct, endless, main-and-tail and gravity haulage systems; pull and power calculations; safety devices — Lilly controller, stop blocks, runaway switches, drag, manholes and refuge holes. Locomotive Haulage: trolley-wire, diesel, battery and flameproof locomotives; track laying and maintenance; mine cars and tubs; productivity calculations for haulage systems.
unit3_text: [08 Hours] Conveyors, Aerial Ropeways & Hoisting Systems Belt Conveyors: construction and main components — drums, idlers, pulleys, fabric and steel-cord belting; drive arrangements; tensioning devices (gravity, screw, hydraulic take-up); loading and discharge arrangements; safety and sequence-control devices; capacity and power calculations; splicing and maintenance. Chain Conveyors: armoured face conveyor (AFC) and panzer conveyor — construction, drive units, chain types and applicability at longwall faces; scraper-chain and shaker conveyors — construction and application. Aerial Ropeways: monocable and bicable systems; construction, layout, rope-tensioning and applications. Hoisting — Shaft Arrangement: headgear, shaft fittings; cages, skips and their suspension gear; detaching hooks; principal safety devices.
unit4_text: [09 Hours] Winding Systems and Face / Development Machinery Drum Winders: cylindrical and conical drums; winding cycles; mechanical and electrical braking (dynamic, regenerative and plugging). Electric Winders: AC and DC drives; speed control (overview); safety circuits and interlocks. Koepe Winding: ground-mounted and tower-mounted Koepe winders; single and multi-rope friction winding; comparison with drum winding. Winding Calculations: torque–time and power–time diagrams; horse-power requirement; selection of winder for given duty cycle. Drilling Machines: jack-hammers, jumbos, drifters and wagon drills; rotary coal drills; DTH and rotary blast-hole drills for opencast mining; selection criteria and productivity assessment. Coal Cutting & Cutter Loaders: conventional coal cutters and ploughs; single-ended and double-ended ranging-drum shearer (DERDS); interface with powered supports. Road Headers: boom-type road headers; rock-tool interaction; selection based on rock strength. Underground Loading & Transport: rocker shovel, gathering-arm loader, side-discharge loader (SDL), load-haul-dump (LHD), shuttle cars and underground trucks; productivity calculation; continuous miner systems. Surface Mining Equipment: rope shovel, hydraulic excavator, dragline (with range-diagram concept), bucket-wheel excavator, continuous surface miner, scrapers, dozers, front-end loaders; productivity calculation for shovel–dumper combination.
unit5_text: [08 Hours] Mine Drainage Pumps and Comminution Machinery Mine Drainage: sources of mine water; drainage planning; dewatering of opencast and underground mines. Types of Mine Pumps: reciprocating, centrifugal (single-stage and multi-stage), turbine, submersible, sinking pumps and sludge pumps; pump fittings and ranging arrangements. Pump Characteristics: head–discharge, power and efficiency curves; net positive suction head (NPSH) and cavitation; series and parallel operation; pump selection for given duty. Comminution Theories: Rittinger's, Kick's and Bond's laws; energy considerations and grindability indices. Crushers: jaw, gyratory, cone and roll crushers — construction, operation and selection criteria. Grinding Mills: ball, rod, tube and pebble mills; critical speed; open and closed-circuit grinding (overview).

co1_text: Explain the types, causes and investigation of mine accidents, accident statistics, and the essential elements of a mine safety-management system.
co2_text: Analyse the hazards arising from mine gases, fires and explosions, and select appropriate detection, monitoring and control measures.
co3_text: Apply dust-control, illumination, inundation-control and occupational-health measures to safeguard the health and safety of mine workers.
co4_text: Apply fault-tree analysis, probabilistic risk analysis and reliability concepts to identify, assess and manage risks in mines.
co5_text: Explain the statutory framework, rescue and recovery practice, and disaster-management measures applicable to Indian mines.
unit1_text: [08 Hours] Mine Accidents, Accident Analysis and Safety Management Mine Accidents: occupational hazards of mining; accidents in mines — different types and classification; accident investigation; accident proneness; basic causes of accident occurrence; place-wise and cause-wise analysis. Accident Statistics & Costs: frequency and severity rates of accidents; accident-data analysis and assessment; relation between accidents and efficiency; direct and indirect cost of accidents. Safety Management: creating and maintaining safety awareness; ZAP and MAP; job safety analysis; safety meetings and committees; management’s role and responsibility; introduction to risk-based safety and health management systems; safety management plan; measures for improving safety in mines.
unit2_text: [08 Hours] Underground Hazards I — Mine Gases, Fires and Explosions Mine Gases: composition of the mine atmosphere; production, properties and physiological effects of mine gases; sampling and analysis of mine air; methane content and methane layering; methane drainage; flame safety lamp and methanometers; radon and its daughter products; continuous monitoring of gases. Mine Fires: causes and classification of mine fires; spontaneous combustion — mechanism, stages and susceptibility indices; factors affecting spontaneous heating; detection and prevention; dealing with mine fires by direct and indirect methods; fire stoppings and sealing-off; re-opening of sealed-off areas; fires in coal stacks and waste dumps. Mine Explosions: firedamp and coal-dust explosions — causes, mechanism and prevention; explosive limits; stone-dust and water barriers; explosions in opencast workings; investigation after an explosion.
unit3_text: [08 Hours] Underground Hazards II — Dust, Inundation, Illumination and Occupational Health Airborne Dust: generation, dispersion, measurement and control of airborne respirable dust; sampling instruments and methods, duration and interval of sampling; prevention and suppression of dust; physiological effects of dust and dust-related diseases (pneumoconiosis, silicosis). Inundation: causes and prevention of inundation; precautions and techniques in approaching old workings; dewatering of waterlogged workings; safety boring apparatus and pattern of holes; design and construction of water dams. Illumination & Occupational Health: standards of illumination for underground and opencast workings; cap lamps; lamp-room layout and organisation; photometry and illumination survey; comfort conditions, first aid and ambulance; miners’ occupational diseases — causes, nature and preventive measures; preventive medical examinations and compensable diseases.
unit4_text: [08 Hours] Risk Assessment and Safety-Engineering Techniques Risk Assessment: principles of risk assessment; hazard identification; risk and hazard control; risk and hazard evaluation; data collection for identified health risks; exposure assessment and risk characterisation; methods of risk assessment. Fault-Tree Analysis: introduction and methodology; symbols and Boolean techniques; qualitative analysis; computerised methods; statistical analysis and safety information; systems design. Reliability & Safety Audit: probabilistic risk analysis; reliability evaluation; human factors; safety culture; safety audit and its application to mine-safety problems.
unit5_text: [08 Hours] Mine Legislation, Rescue, Recovery and Disaster Management Mine Legislation: the Mines Act, 1952; the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017; the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961; statutory controls and directions; spot and regular inspections; enforcement of standards and penalties for violations; role of the Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS); safety campaigns and Safety Week. Rescue & Recovery: rescue equipment and its uses; classification of rescue apparatus; resuscitation; rescue stations and rescue rooms; organisation of rescue work; emergency preparedness and response systems; Mines Rescue Rules and Mines Vocational Training Rules. Disaster Management: identification of causes of mine disasters; preventive action; disaster management and mitigation; typical cases of mine disasters in India; recommendations of inquiry committees on safety and health issues.

co1_text: Explain the essential elements, principles and strategies of mine automation and the working of autonomous mining, fleet-management and remote-operation systems.
co2_text: Make use of automated communication, tracking, sensing and virtual-reality technologies for implementing automation and ensuring safe operations in mines.
co3_text: Apply descriptive and inferential statistics and fundamental machine-learning concepts to analyse mining data.
co4_text: Analyse mining data using supervised learning, artificial neural networks and deep-learning techniques.
co5_text: Apply unsupervised learning, big-data analytics and artificial intelligence to mining decision-making and optimisation problems.
unit1_text: [08 Hours] Foundations of Mine Automation and Autonomous Systems Automation Fundamentals: essential elements of an automated system; automation in the mine production system; principles and strategies of automation; introduction to automation productivity and levels of automation. Autonomous Mining Systems: autonomous haulage systems (AHS); automated drilling systems; tele-remote and autonomous operating modes; selection considerations for autonomous equipment. Fleet Management & Remote Operations: Fleet Management Systems — Truck Dispatch System (TDS), Computerised Maintenance Management System (CMMS) and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) for the mining industry; mine remote operations and control; mining robotics and “armchair mining”; remote operating centres.
unit2_text: [08 Hours] Sensing, Communication, Tracking and Virtual-Reality Technologies Automated Communication & Tracking Technologies: proximity-detection systems; GNSS/UPS positioning; radar systems; RFID and geo-fencing; CCD cameras and machine vision; image processing; SCADA architecture and its applications in mines. Virtual Reality & Simulation: virtual-reality applications in mining; mining-equipment concept development; mine-safety training applications; mining-operation simulations and visualisation of the mining process for safe operations.
unit3_text: [08 Hours] Statistical Foundations and Introduction to Machine Learning Descriptive Statistics: measures of central tendency and dispersion; data summarisation and visualisation; probability and probability distributions (discrete and continuous) relevant to mining data. Inferential Statistics: sampling and estimation; hypothesis testing; regression analysis; analysis of variance (ANOVA); interpretation of results for mining problems. Introduction to Machine Learning: basic concepts, terminology and the learning workflow; supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning; the data-analytics pipeline for mining applications.
unit4_text: [08 Hours] Supervised Learning, Neural Networks and Deep Learning Supervised Learning: classification and regression; feature engineering; training, validation and testing; the bias–variance trade-off; model-evaluation metrics. Artificial Neural Networks: the perceptron and multilayer networks; activation functions; the back-propagation algorithm; network training and regularisation. Deep Learning: deep network architectures (overview); representation and feature learning; representative applications of deep learning to mining and geoscience data.
unit5_text: [08 Hours] Unsupervised Learning, Big-Data Analytics and AI Applications in Mining Unsupervised Learning: clustering techniques; pattern and structure discovery in unlabelled mining data; dimensionality reduction (overview). Big-Data Analytics: characteristics and challenges of big data; data acquisition, storage and management; analytics frameworks and pipelines for large-scale mining data. Applications in Mining: application of big-data analytics and artificial intelligence in mining — predictive maintenance, production and energy optimisation, safety analytics and decision-support systems.

co1_text: Classify mineral resources and reserves as per UNFC; carry out sampling and grade-reserve estimation for mineral deposits.
co2_text: Apply standard methods of mine valuation (Hoskold's, Morkill's, present-value) and compute depreciation and capital recovery for mining assets.
co3_text: Evaluate mining investment proposals using discounted and non-discounted cash flow methods and perform sensitivity analysis.
co4_text: Explain principles of financial management of mining enterprises and apply provisions of mineral taxation under MMDR Act and related rules.
co5_text: Prepare profit-and-loss account, balance sheet and cost-of-production statements; demonstrate awareness of National Mineral Policy and sustainable mining.
unit1_text: [06 Hours] Mineral Resources, Reserves and Sampling Resource and Reserve Classification: concepts; IBM and UNFC frameworks; JORC and CRIRSCO codes; measured, indicated and inferred resources; proved, probable and possible reserves. Sampling and Statistical Analysis: grab, channel, chip, bulk and drill-core sampling; sample preparation and reduction; salting and precautions; statistical treatment — mean, variance and standard error of grade. Grade and Reserve Estimation: cut-off grade and break-even grade; reserve estimation by cross-section, polygonal, triangular and inverse-distance methods; introduction to geostatistics and kriging; grade-tonnage curve.
unit2_text: [07 Hours] Mine Valuation Valuation Fundamentals: objectives and scope of mine valuation; factors affecting mine value; valuation for sale, taxation and mortgage; distinction between mine, accounting and market valuation. Methods of Mine Valuation: present-value method; Hoskold's, Morkill's and O'Donahue formulae; replacement-cost and comparative methods; relative merits and limitations. Life and Capacity of a Mine: Taylor's rule for optimum capacity; relationship between reserve, capacity and life; effect of cut-off grade on life and capacity. Depreciation and Capital Recovery: straight-line, declining-balance, sum-of-years-digits, sinking-fund and production-unit methods; amortization of intangibles; redemption of capital; depletion allowance.
unit3_text: [09 Hours] Discounted Cash Flow Analysis Time Value of Money: compounding and discounting; present value, future value, annuity and perpetuity; effect of compounding frequency. Cash Flow Analysis: project cash flow diagrams; project life cycle — exploration, development, production and closure; treatment of escalation, inflation and working capital; tax-affected cash flow. Investment Appraisal Methods: non-discounted methods — payback period and accounting rate of return; discounted methods — NPV, IRR, discounted payback, profitability index, B/C ratio, modified IRR; conflict between NPV and IRR for ranking. Sensitivity and Risk Analysis: one-way sensitivity (spider and tornado diagrams); scenario analysis; Monte-Carlo simulation (overview); risk-adjusted discount rate. Project Selection: ranking of mutually exclusive projects; capital rationing; replacement decisions; case studies on mining-project appraisal.
unit4_text: [09 Hours] Financial Management and Mineral Taxation Business Organization and Financing: forms of business organization; memorandum and articles of association; sources of short-term and long-term capital for mining enterprises. Capital Structure: equity shares, preference shares, debentures, retained earnings and term loans; cost of capital; weighted average cost of capital (WACC); leverage. Break-Even and Inventory: break-even chart, break-even point, margin of safety and contribution margin; ABC analysis, Economic Order Quantity (EOQ), reorder level and safety stock. Mineral Taxation: royalty (tonnage and ad-valorem); dead rent; cess — District Mineral Foundation (DMF) and National Mineral Exploration Trust (NMET); income tax on mining; GST impact; MMDR Act 1957 (as amended in 2015 and 2021); Mineral Concession Rules 2016. Mineral Pricing: factors governing mineral prices; primary versus secondary markets; price volatility and cyclical nature of the mineral economy; long-term contracts versus spot markets; commodity exchanges.
unit5_text: [05 Hours] Financial Statements and Mineral Economics in Practice Book-Keeping Essentials: double-entry system; journal, ledger and subsidiary books; trial balance; rectification of errors. Financial Statements: preparation of profit-and-loss account and balance sheet; key financial ratios — current ratio, debt-equity, ROCE and earnings per share. Cost of Production: cost classification — fixed, variable, direct, indirect and overhead; cost per tonne; cost centres in a mine. Mineral Economics in Industry: National Mineral Policy 2019; pre-feasibility, feasibility and bankable feasibility studies; sustainable mining and ESG reporting (overview).

unit1_text:
I
Introduction to Madhyasth Darshan and its Basics Need
to study Madhyasth Darshan; introduction, basic
formulations of the darshan; the complete expanse of
study and the natural outcome of living according to the
darshan.
unit2_text:
II
Submergence of Nature in Space
The ever-present existence in the form of nature
submerged in space; nature classified into two
categories – material and consciousness, and four
orders; the form, property, natural characteristic and
selforganization of the four orders, General direction
and process of evolution in the nature/ existence.
unit3_text:
III
Human Being as an indivisible part of Nature
Human being as an indivisible part of nature; various
types (five classes) of human beings; human being in
the combination of self and body; purpose of self as
realization, prosperity for the body; need of behavior
and work for attaining the goals of realization and
prosperity
unit4_text:
IV
Fulfillment of human goal of realization and prosperity
Following natural, social and psychological principles
for actualizing the human goal; form of conducive
society and order for such practices, study process-
achieving realization through self-study and practice
while living in such a society (social order).
unit5_text:
V
Human Conduct based on Madhyasth Darshan
Description of such a realized self, continuity of
happiness, peace, satisfaction and bliss through
realization, conduct of a realized human being.
Possibility of finding solutions to present day problems
(such as inequality of rich and poor, man and woman
etc.) in the light of it.

unit1_text:
Introduction: 
The basic human aspirations and their fulfillment through Right understanding and 
Resolution; All-encompassing Resolution for a Human Being, its details and solution of 
problems in the light of Resolution.
unit2_text:
Understanding Human being and its expansion: 
The domain of right understanding starts from understanding the human being (the knower, 
the experience and the doer); and extends up to understanding nature/existence – its 
interconnectedness and co-existence; and finally understanding the role of human being in 
existence (human conduct).
unit3_text:
Activities of the Self: 
Understanding the human being comprehensively is the first step and the core theme of this 
course; human being as co-existence of the self and the body; the activities and potentialities of 
the self; Reasons for harmony/contradiction in the self.
unit4_text:
Understanding Co-existence with other orders: 
The need and the process of inner evolution (through self-exploration, selfawareness and 
self-evaluation)- particularly awakening to activities of the Self: Realization, Understanding and 
Contemplation in the Self (Realization of Co-Existence, Understanding of Harmony in 
Nature and Contemplation of Participation of Human in this harmony/ order leading to 
comprehensive knowledge about the existence).
unit5_text:
Expansion of harmony from self to entire existence: 
Understanding different aspects of All-encompassing Resolution (understanding, wisdom, 
science etc.), Holistic way of living for Human Being with All-encompassing Resolution 
covering all four dimensions of human endeavour viz., realization, thought, behavior and 
work (participation in the larger order) leading to harmony at all levels from self to Nature 
and entire Existence.

co2_text: Describe and use the modern tools of quality management

unit1_text:
Unit‐1:
Quality‐ Quality: Definition, History, Importance, Cost of Quality, Approaches of Quality Management, Hierarchy of Quality management: Inspection & Test, Quality Control, Quality Assurance, Total Quality Management
unit2_text:
Unit‐2:
Quality Control‐ Statistical Quality Control‐ SQC tools, Benefits of SQC, Attributes & variables, Problems on FD curve & ND curve. Control chart for variable, Control chart patterns, Process capability. Problems on x & R chart and Process capability. Control chart for attribute, Problems on p, c charts. Sampling: Definition, types of sampling, importance, benefits, and limitations of sampling.
unit3_text:
Unit‐3:
Modern Concepts related to Quality Management‐ Quality Assurance (QA): Introduction, Definition, Management principles in QA, Forms of QA, QA in different stages. Quality planning, QA program, QA aspect, Quality in material management. ISO: Introduction, Benefits of ISO. Total Quality Management: Definition, Models of TQM, Elements of TQM, Principles of TQM, JIT, Training for Quality management. Quality Improvement Programme: Histogram, Charts, Brain‐storming, Cause & Effect diagram, Pareto analysis, Quality Circle, Introduction to Six Sigma and Taguchi concepts
unit4_text:
Unit‐4:
Reliability‐ Definition, Factor of safety and reliability, Reliability analysis procedure; Basic probability theory, Central limit theorem; Functions of random variables, Probability distribution functions, density functions for different types of discrete and continuous variables, mean, mode and median; Failure rate versus time, reliability and hazard functions and different distributions, Estimation of failure rate, Expected residual life, Series, parallel and mixed systems, complex systems, Reliability enhancement.
unit5_text:
Unit‐5:
Industrial Safety‐ Introduction, key concepts, terminologies, and safety quantification, safety by design; Hazard identification techniques (e.g. HAZOP, FMEA, etc.); Fault tree and event tree analysis (qualitative & quantitative); Bow‐tie and quantitative risk assessment (QRA); Safety function deployment; Safety vs reliability – quantification of basic events (repair to failure, repair‐failure‐repair, and combined processes); Systems safety quantification (e.g. truth tables, structure functions, minimal cut sets); Human error analysis and safety; Accident investigation and analysis.

unit4_text:

Cohesive energy, cohesive energy density, solubility parameter, determination of solubility parameter of polymers – Prediction of solubility parameter- Effect of polymer structure on solubility in solvents and oils - Influence of structure in prediction of flame retardancy, water repellency – Chemical resistance of polymers - Polymer toxicity.

unit1_text: Chemistry of Textile Fibres: Classification of textile fibres; natural fibres (cotton, wool, silk, jute) and their chemical composition; synthetic fibres (nylon, polyester, acrylic); physical and chemical properties of fibres; moisture absorption and swelling; fibre morphology and structure-property relationship.

Introduction of thermodynamics and Heat Transfer, Modes of Heat Transfer: Conduction, convection and radiation, Effect of temperature on thermal conductivity of different types of materials, Introduction to combined heat transfer mechanism, General differential heat conduction equation in the rectangular, cylindrical and spherical coordinate systems, Initial and system boundary conditions.
Steady State one‐dimensional Heat conduction (3 Hours)
Simple and Composite Systems in rectangular, cylindrical and spherical coordinates with and without energy generation, Concept of thermal resistance, Analogy between heat and electricity flow, Thermal contact resistance and over‐all heat transfer coefficient, Critical radius of insulation for cylindrical, and spherical bodies.
unit2_text:
Fins (3 Hours)
Heat transfer through extended surfaces and its classification, Fins of uniform cross‐sectional area, Error in measurement of temperature of thermometer wells.
Transient Conduction (3 Hours)
Transient heat conduction, Lumped capacitance method, Time constant, Unsteady state heat conduction in one dimension only, Heisler charts and their applications.
unit3_text:
Forced Convection (5 Hours)
Basic concepts: Hydrodynamic boundary layer, Thermal boundary layer, Approximate integral boundary layer analysis, Analogy between momentum and heat transfer in turbulent flow over a flat surface, Mixed boundary layer, Flow over a flat plate, Flow across a single cylinder and a sphere, Flow inside ducts, Thermal entrance region, Empirical heat transfer relations, Relation between fluid friction and heat transfer, Liquid metal heat transfer.
Natural Convection (5 Hours)
Physical mechanism of natural convection, Buoyant force, Empirical heat transfer relations for natural convection over vertical planes and cylinders, horizontal plates, cylinders and sphere, combined free and forced convection, Effect of turbulence.
unit4_text:
Thermal Radiation (8 Hours)
Basic concepts of radiation, Radiation properties of surfaces, Black body radiation Planck’s law, Wein’s displacement law, Stefan‐Boltzmann law, Kirchhoff’s law, Gray body, Shape factor, Black‐body radiation, Radiation exchange between diffuse non‐black bodies in an enclosure, Radiation shields, Radiation combined with conduction and convection; Absorption and emission in gaseous medium; Solar radiation; Greenhouse effect, Radiation network analysis.
unit5_text:
Heat Exchanger (5 Hours)
Different types of heat exchangers, Fouling factors, Overall heat transfer coefficient, Logarithmic mean temperature difference (LMTD) method, Effectiveness‐number of transfer unit (NTU) method and Compact Heat Exchangers.
Condensation and Boiling (3 Hours)
Introduction of condensation phenomena, Heat transfer relations for laminar film condensation on vertical surfaces and on outside& inside of a horizontal tube, Effect of non‐condensable gases, Drop wise condensation, Heat pipes, Boiling modes, pool boiling, Hysteresis in boiling curve, Forced convection boiling.
Introduction to Mass Transfer (2 Hours)
Introduction of Fick's law of diffusion, Steady state equimolar counter diffusion, Steady state diffusion through a stagnant gas film, Heat and Mass Transfer Analogy ‐Convective Mass Transfer Correlations

Part A:  Sports/Games

Some form of Athletics would be compulsory for all students, unless restricted due 
to medical / physical reasons. In addition to this, student has to opt for at least one 
game out of the remaining mentioned below.  
A fair theoretical knowledge and a reasonable amount of field / site practice of the 
chosen games will be essential. 

1. Athletics 

Compulsory 

  
2. Volleyball 
             
3. Basketball 
4. Handball  
5. Football 
6. Badminton 
7. Kabaddi 
8. Kho-kho 
9. Table tennis 
10. Cricket
unit2_text:
Part B: Yoga

a. Introduction of Yoga 
Introduction of Yoga, Origin of Yoga, Aims and Objective of Yoga, Patanjal Yoga 
darshan, Hathyoga, Gheranda Samhita, Karmyoga, Gyanyoga. 

b. Asanas, Pranayam and Meditation Practices  
Meaning of Asanas, Objective of Asanas, rules and regulations of Asanas and 
Pranayams, Types of Yogasana  
Yogic postures: Standing Posture, Sitting posture, Supine posture, Prone posture, 
balancing Postures, Pranayam according to Patanjali and Hath Yoga, Meditation 
Mudras 

c. Science of Yoga 
Physiological effects of Asanas- Pranayama and meditation,stress management 
and yoga, Mental health and yoga practice, Health and Personality 
Development. 
Genral Guidelines. 
1. Institutes must assign minimum of three periods in the Time Table for the 
activities of Sports/Yoga. 
2. Institutes must provide field/facility and offer a minimum of five choices of the 
Games/Sports. 
3. Institutes are required to provide sports instructor / yoga teacher to mentor 
the students. 
4. Student must be made familiar with the terminologies, rules/regulations,  
dimension/ marking of the play field/area and general knowledge of national/ 
international level facts/figures related to the chosen game. 
Assessment: 
The Institute must assign coordinator/ subject teacher for the subject,  for every 
batch/group of the students,  who would be responsible for coordinating the required 
activities and keep watch on the level of student’s participation in the chosen game.  
Coordinator/mentor would be responsible for the award of the sessional marks based upon 
following components.  
1. Level of understanding and general awareness  ( 20 %) 
2.  Involvements in the Practice Sessions 

(50 %) 
3. Regularity, Sincerity and Discipline  

(20 %) 
4. Participation in University level / District level / State level / National 
Level events    



(10 %)

Introduction: 
The basic human aspirations and their fulfillment through Right understanding and 
Resolution; All-encompassing Resolution for a Human Being, its details and solution of 
problems in the light of Resolution.
unit2_text:
Understanding Human being and its expansion: 
The domain of right understanding starts from understanding the human being (the knower, 
the experience and the doer); and extends up to understanding nature/existence – its 
interconnectedness and co-existence; and finally understanding the role of human being in 
existence (human conduct).
unit3_text:
Activities of the Self: 
Understanding the human being comprehensively is the first step and the core theme of this 
course; human being as co-existence of the self and the body; the activities and potentialities 
of the self; Reasons for harmony/contradiction in the self.
unit4_text:
Understanding Co-existence with other orders: 
The need and the process of inner evolution (through self-exploration, selfawareness and 
self-evaluation)- particularly awakening to activities of the Self: Realization, Understanding 
and Contemplation in the Self (Realization of Co-Existence, Understanding of Harmony in 
Nature and Contemplation of Participation of Human in this harmony/ order leading to 
comprehensive knowledge about the existence).
unit5_text:
Expansion of harmony from self to entire existence: 
Understanding different aspects of All-encompassing Resolution (understanding, wisdom, 
science etc.), Holistic way of living for Human Being with All-encompassing Resolution 
covering all four dimensions of human endeavour viz., realization, thought, behavior and 
work (participation in the larger order) leading to harmony at all levels from self to Nature 
and entire Existence.

unit1_text:
Introduction to Sankhya, Yoga and Vedanta Darshan and their Basics 
Need to study Sankhya, Yoga and Vedanta Darshan; the origin of the three philosophies,
their basic principles and scope for further reading.
unit2_text:
Sankhya Darshan 
Sankhya Darshan- the nature of Purush and Prakriti, 8 types of prakriti (pradhan,
mahattatva, ahankar and five tanmatras- sound, touch, form, taste and smell) and their 16
evolutes (vicar); pramana (pratyaksha, anumana and agama), bondage and salvation
(liberation), the principle of satkaryavad, sense organs, work organs, trigunatmak prakriti
unit3_text:
YogaDarshan 
Yoga Darshan- the steps of Ashtanga yoga (yama, niyama,aasana, pranayama, pratyahara,
dharana, dhyan and samadhi) and the challenges in following them, afflictions (klesha)-
avidya, asmita, raga, dvesha, abhinivesh, different types of vritti (pramana, viparyaya,
vikalp, nidra, smriti), the process of nirodha of vritti; maitri, karuna, mudita, upeksha;
description of yama, niyama, aasana and pranayaama; kriyayoga –tapa, swadhyaya and
ishwar-pranidhana, different steps of samadhi, different types of sanyama, vivekakhyati,
pragya.
unit4_text:
Vedanta Darshan 
Vedanta Darshan- Nature of Brahma and Prakriti, Methods of Upasana; adhyasa and
sanskar; nature of Atma, description of existence, principle of karma-phala, description of
pancha kosha, different nature of paramatma/brahma, Ishwar, Four qualifications (Sadhan-
chatushtay).
unit5_text:
Purpose and Program for a Human Being based on the Three Darshan 
The purpose and program of a human being living on the basis of the three darshanas, clarity
and practice of human values and human conduct, the natural outcome of such a program on
society, nature and tradition. possibility of finding solutions to present day problems in the
light of it.

unit1_text:
Introduction to Vedic Darśana and Nyāya Darśana (Philosophy of Indian Logic and Reasoning)
Introduction to Vedic literature, need to study Vedic Darśana; its origin and subject matter. Introduction to Nyāya Darśana, 16 padārthas (pramāṇa, prameya, saṃśaya, prayojana, dṛṣṭānta, siddhānta, avayava, tarka, nirṇaya, vāda, jalpa, vitaṇḍā, hetuābhāsa, chala, jāti, nigrahasthāna) paṃcāvayava prakriyā (pratijñā, hetu, udāharaṇa, upanaya, nigamana).
unit2_text:
Vaiśeṣika Darśana (Philosophy of Matter)
Introduction to Vaiśeṣika Darśana, definition of Dharma, abhyudaya, niḥśreyasa; 6 padārthas (dravya, guṇa, karma, sāmānya, viśeśa, samavāya) – their definition, characteristics and relationship; nitya-anitya; cause-effect relationships; dṛṣṭa-adṛṣṭa karma phala; mindful dāna; śucitā-aśucitā; reasons of rāga-dveśa, avidyā, sukha-duḥkha, etc. and how to get rid of them.
unit3_text:
Sāṃkhya-Yoga Darśana (Philosophy of Spirituality)
Sāṃkhya Darśana- Puruṣārtha, the nature of Puruṣa and Prakṛti, 24 elements of Prakṛti, bondage and salvation (liberation), the principle of satkāryavāda, triguṇātmaka prakṛti.Yoga Darśana- the steps of Aṣṭāṃga yoga (yama, niyama, āsana, prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhāraṇā, dhyāna and samādhi) and the challenges in following them, afflictions (kleṣa)- avidyā, asmitā, rāga, dveṣa, abhiniveśa, different types of vṛttis (pramāṇa, viparyaya, vikalpa, nidrā, smṛti), the process of nirodha of vṛttis; maitri, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā; description of yama, niyama, āsana and praṇayāma; kriyāyoga– tapa, svādhyāya and īśvara-praṇidhāna; different steps of samādhi, different types of saṃyama, vivekakhyāti, prajñā.
Vedanta Darshan
Vedanta Darshan- Nature of Brahma and Prakriti, Methods of Upasana; adhyasaand sanskar; nature of Atma, description of existence, principle of karma-phala, description o pancha kosha, different nature of paramatma/brahma, Ishwar, Four qualifications (Sadhan chatushtay).
unit4_text:
Upaniṣad and Vedanta Darśana (Philosophy of God)
Introduction to Upaniṣads and Vedanta Darśana; Īśopaniṣad – Idea of renouncement, Karma Yoga, balance of Vidyā-Avidyā and Prakṛti-Vikṛti; Tattirīyopaniṣad – Different names of the God and their meaning, parting message of Guru to the graduating student (Śikṣāvallī), Nature of Brahma and Prakṛti, Methods of Upāsanā; Nature of Ātmā, Description of existence, principle of karma-phala, description of paṃca kośa, nature of mukti, process and way to achieve it, antaḥkaraṇa-śuddhi, different characteristics of paramātmā/brahma, Īśvara, Four qualifications (Sādhana-catuṣṭaya)
unit5_text:
Purpose and Program for a Human Being based on the Vedic Darśana
The purpose and program of a human being living on the basis of the Vedic Darśana, clarity and practice of human values and human conduct, the natural outcome of such a program on society, nature and tradition. Vedic system of living in a society - the idea of vratas and varaṇa (freedom of choice with commitment), Varṇa System, Āśrama System, Paṃca Mahāyajṇa, 16 Saṃskāras, etc.

co1_text: Understand the basic concepts of contract law including offer, acceptance, consideration, capacity, free consent, void agreements, performance, discharge, and remedies under the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
co2_text: Explain the legal provisions related to special contracts like indemnity and guarantee, including types of guarantee, rights and liabilities of surety and co-surety, and discharge of surety.
co3_text: Analyze the concepts of bailment and pledge along with rights and duties of bailor and bailee, and understand the legal framework of agency, including formation, classification, and termination of agency.

Unit- I (Hours 10) 
  
Indian Contract Act 1872 – Contract - Definition & Concept; Agreement - Offer & Acceptance;

Fraud, Misrepresentation, Mistake - Bilateral and Unilateral; Void Agreements - Agreements in Restraint 
of Marriage, Agreement in Restraint of Trade, Uncertain Agreements, Agreements in Restraint of Legal 
Proceedings, Wagering and Contingent Agreements and Contracts; Quasi Contracts; Performance and 
Discharge of Contracts; Breach of Contracts and Remedies.
unit2_text:
Unit -II (Hours 08) 
  
Special Contracts Indemnity and Guarantee - Meaning, Nature and Features, Types of Guarantee, 
Provisions related to different types of Guarantee, Surety and Co-surety - Rights and Liabilities, Discharge 
of Surety.
unit3_text:
Unit -III (Hours 08) 
  
Bailment and Pledge: Rights and Duties of Bailor and Bailee, Termination of Bailment; Agency: 
Creation of Agency, Classification of Agents, Relationship between Principal and Agent, Rights, Duties 
and Liabilities of Agent and Principal, Termination of Agency.
unit4_text:
Unit –IV (Hours 06) 
  
Contract of Sale of Goods: The Sale of Goods Act 1930- Introduction, Contract of Sale, Sale and 
Agreement to Sale, Kinds of Goods, Conditions and Warranties - Implied Conditions and Warranties, 
Doctrine of ‘Caveat Emptor’, Transfer of Property, Delivery of Goods, Duties of the Seller and the Buyer, 
Unpaid Seller’s Remedies,
unit5_text:
Unit-V (Hours 08) 
  
Partnership - Law of partnership: Definition, essentials of partnership, registration of partnership, kinds 
of partners, rights, liabilities of partners, dissolution of partnership.

unit1_text:
UNIT –I (7 sessions) Production Concepts: 
Introduction, meaning, nature and scope of production and operations management. Difference 
between production and operations management. Productivity, factors affecting productivity and 
productivity measurement. Work study— Method study and work measurement. Production 
Technology – Types of manufacturing processes. Plant location and types of plant layout.
unit2_text:
UNIT –II (8 sessions) Operations Concepts: 
Services scenario in India, difference between product and service, characteristics of services, 
classification of services, product and service design, factors affecting service design, service 
designing process, service blueprinting, service capacity planning. Dimensions of quality in services, 
understanding service quality gap, measuring service quality using SERVQUAL model. Case 
Studies
unit3_text:
UNIT-III (10 sessions) Material and Inventory Management: 
Types of production planning, process of production planning and control (PPC) – routing, 
scheduling and loading. Master production schedule, aggregate production planning. Types of 
inventories, inventory control techniques- EOQ, ABC, VED, FSN, HML and SDE (Simple 
numerical problems on Inventory control techniques). Just-in-time (JIT) and KANBAN. Case 
Studies
unit4_text:
UNIT-IV (8 sessions) Supply Chain Management: 
Overview of supply chain management, conceptual model of SCM, supply chain drivers, measuring 
supply chain performance, core and reverse supply chain, global supply chain, inbound and 
outbound logistics, Bullwhip effect in SCM, push and pull systems, lean manufacturing, agile 
manufacturing, role of IT in SCM. Demand forecasting in supply chain— 
Simple moving average method, weighted moving average method, linear regression and 
exponential smoothing method. Case Studies
unit5_text:
UNIT-V (7 sessions) Productivity and Quality: 
TQM, Deming’s 14 principles, Juran’s quality triology, PDCA cycle, KAIZEN, quality circles, 
7QC tools and its 7 new management tools, ISO 9000-2000 clauses, six sigma, Total 
Productive Maintenance (TPM), 5S. Case Studies

unit1_text:
UNIT-1: Course Introduction - Need, Basic Guidelines, Content and Process for Value Education (6 Hours) 
Understanding the need, basic guidelines, content and process for Value Education, Self-Exploration–what is it? - its content and process; ‘Natural Acceptance’ and Experiential Validation- as the mechanism for self-exploration, Continuous Happiness and Prosperity- A look at basic Human Aspirations, Right understanding, Relationship and Physical Facilities- the basic requirements for fulfillment of aspirations of every human being with their correct priority, Understanding Happiness and Prosperity correctly- A critical appraisal of the current scenario, Method to fulfill the above human aspirations: understanding and living in harmony at various levels.
unit2_text:
UNIT-2: Understanding Harmony in the Human Being - Harmony in Myself (7 Hours) 
Understanding human being as a co-existence of the sentient ‘I’ and the material ‘Body’, Understanding the needs of Self (‘I’) and ‘Body’ - Sukh and Suvidha, Understanding the Body as an instrument of ‘I’ (I being the doer, seer and enjoyer), Understanding the characteristics and activities of ‘I’ and harmony in ‘I’, Understanding the harmony of I with the Body: Sanyam and Swasthya; correct appraisal of Physical needs, meaning of Prosperity in detail, Programs to ensure Sanyam and Swasthya.
unit3_text:
UNIT-3: Understanding Harmony in the Family and Society- Harmony in Human-Human Relationship (8 Hours) 
Understanding harmony in the Family- the basic unit of human interaction, Understanding values in human-human relationship; meaning of Nyaya and program for its fulfillment to ensure Ubhay-tripti; Trust (Vishwas) and Respect (Samman) as the foundational values of relationship, Understanding the meaning of Vishwas; Difference between intention and competence, Understanding the meaning of Samman, Difference between respect and differentiation; the other salient values in relationship, Understanding the harmony in the society (society being an extension of family): Samadhan, Samridhi, Abhay, Sah-astitva as comprehensive Human Goals, Visualizing a universal harmonious order in society- Undivided Society (AkhandSamaj), Universal Order (Sarvabhaum Vyawastha )- from family to world family!.
unit4_text:
UNIT-4: Understanding Harmony in the Nature and Existence - Whole existence as Co-existence (8 Hours) 
Understanding the harmony in the Nature, Interconnectedness and mutual fulfilment among the four orders of nature- recyclability and self-regulation in nature, Understanding Existence as Co-existence (Sah-astitva) of mutually interacting units in all-pervasive space, Holistic perception of harmony at all levels of existence.
unit5_text:
UNIT-5: Implications of the above Holistic Understanding of Harmony on Professional Ethics ( 9 Hours) 
Natural acceptance of human values, Definitiveness of Ethical Human Conduct, Basis for Humanistic Education, Humanistic Constitution and Humanistic Universal Order, Competence in Professional Ethics: a) Ability to utilize the professional competence for augmenting universal human order, b) Ability to identify the scope and characteristics of people-friendly and eco-friendly production systems, technologies and management models, Case studies of typical holistic technologies, management models and production systems, Strategy for transition from the present state to Universal Human Order: a) At the level of individual: as socially and ecologically responsible engineers, technologists and managers, b) At the level of society: as mutually enriching institutions and organizations

fraud, IL&FS crisis; governance breakdowns and ethical lapses; lessons from corporate collapses;

unit1_text:
Unit 1: Introduction to International Business and Trade Theories (8 Hours)

Nature, scope, and importance of international business, introduction to EPRG & LPG frameworks, 
major modes of market entry: exporting, joint ventures, FDI, licensing, wholly owned subsidiaries, 
theoretical foundations: classical and modern trade theories, Leontief paradox, PLC theory, national 
competitive advantage, and factor mobility theory.
unit2_text:
Unit 2: Trade Policy & Commercial Instruments (6 Hours)

Instruments of commercial policy: tariffs, quotas, subsidies, non-tariff barriers, economic multiplier 
effects (with numerical examples), trade protectionism, India’s foreign trade policy, Make in India 
initiatives, LPG policy framework.
unit3_text:
Unit 3: Business Environment & Political Economy (10 Hours)

International business environment analysis: PESTEL covering economic, political, cultural, 
technological factors, cultural dimensions: language, religion, communication styles in business 
contexts, political and legal frameworks: systems of governance, legal protection, IPR, and national 
risk factors. Latest updates and cases.
unit4_text:
Unit 4: International Marketing (8 Hours)

Introduction to International Marketing: Definition, scope and importance; Differences between 
domestic and international marketing; EPRG framework (Ethnocentric, Polycentric, Regiocentric, 
Geocentric); Environmental factors affecting international marketing – Political, Economic, Social, 
Cultural, Technological, Legal; Hofstede’s cultural dimensions and their impact on marketing 
decisions; International market research and segmentation; International product and pricing 
decisions. Latest updates and cases.
unit5_text:
Unit 5: International Strategy, Institutions and Operations (8 Hours)

Global business strategy: standardization vs localization, international expansion strategies 
including M&A, alliances, licensing, franchising, international marketing, supply chain and 
logistics management, use of Incoterms, role of trade promotion bodies in India (EXIM Bank, 
ECGC), global institutions and trade agreements: WTO, GATT, IMF, World Bank, TRIPS, 
TRIMS, GATS, regional economic blocs: EU, ASEAN, NAFTA, SAARC, emergence and 
strategies of multinational firms, Indian export promotion schemes and SEZ policies.

co1_text:
Explain the concepts, theories and models of consumer behaviour and their 
relevance to marketing decisions.
co2_text:
Describe the influence of cultural, social, reference-group and family 
factors on consumer choices in diverse markets.
co3_text:
Explain how perception, motivation, learning, personality and attitudes 
shape consumer responses.
co4_text:
Apply consumer decision-making models to interpret buying behaviour in 
traditional and digital marketplaces.
co5_text:
Apply consumer insights to marketing-mix decisions for organisational and 
digital buying situations in the Indian context.
unit1_text:
Module I: Introduction to Consumer Behaviour (7 Hours) 
Concept, nature, scope, and importance of consumer behaviour; relationship between consumer behaviour 
and marketing; consumer value, consumerism and consumer rights; factors influencing consumer 
behaviour; emerging trends in consumer markets; ethical marketing practices; introduction to online 
consumer behaviour and digital consumer journey; overview of organisational buying behaviour.
unit2_text:
Module II: External Influences on Consumer Behaviour (9 Hours) 
Lifestyle analysis and psychographics; AIO (Activities, Interests, Opinions) framework; social class and 
consumption patterns; reference groups and group dynamics; family decision-making and family life 
cycle; role of opinion leaders and influencers; cultural values, subcultures, and cross-cultural influences; 
global and Indian consumer diversity.
unit3_text:
Module III: Internal Psychological Influences (8 Hours) 
Consumer perception and perceptual mapping; learning theories and memory systems; motivation 
theories and their marketing implications; personality and self-concept; consumer involvement; attitude 
formation and change; cognitive dissonance and its impact on post-purchase behaviour; implications for 
branding and communication strategies; case studies.
unit4_text:
Module IV: Consumer Decision-Making Process (9 Hours) 
Concept and stages of decision-making; need recognition, information search, evaluation of alternatives, 
purchase decision, and post-purchase behaviour; situational influences (physical, social, temporal, 
psychological); satisfaction, dissatisfaction, and loyalty formation; traditional and contemporary models 
of consumer decision-making; application of behavioural models in marketing strategy; case studies
unit5_text:
Module V: Digital, Organisational and Strategic Consumer Behaviour (7 Hours) 
Online consumer behaviour and digital decision journey; e-commerce buying behaviour;  consumer 
analytics and behavioural data interpretation; application of consumer insights in segmentation, targeting, 
and positioning; development of customer-centric marketing strategies using behavioural insights; 
emerging trends in AI-driven consumer analytics.

co1_text: Explain the fundamental concepts of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Business Analytics in a managerial context.
co2_text: Apply basic analytics techniques such as charts, dashboards, correlation and trend analysis to business data.

unit1_text: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence: meaning, evolution, scope, and types of AI; AI vs traditional computing; overview of machine learning, deep learning, and data science; role of AI in business decision-making; introduction to business analytics (descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, prescriptive); data-driven decision-making; data lifecycle in organisations; ethical, legal, and managerial challenges of AI adoption.

unit1_text:
Module I: Introduction to GST Framework (7 Hours) 
Concept and evolution of GST; indirect tax structure in India; objectives and features of GST; One Nation 
One Tax concept; GST Council and GSTN; structure of GST (CGST, SGST, UTGST, IGST); GST rates 
and classification; GST registration process including compulsory registration, exemption, cancellation, 
and GSTIN; overview of advantages and limitations of GST system.
unit2_text:
Module II: Levy, Supply and Input Tax Credit (9 Hours) 
Levy and collection of GST; persons/entities liable to pay tax; composition scheme; input tax credit (ITC); 
eligibility, conditions, ineligible credits, and reversal; Input Service Distributor (ISD); tax invoices and 
related documents-credit note, debit note, bill of supply, receipt voucher; payment mechanisms through 
electronic cash, credit, and liability ledgers.
unit3_text:
Module III: GST Returns, Audit and Digital Applications (8 Hours) 
Overview of GST returns; filing procedures and compliance timelines; audit under GST; departmental 
audit procedures and assessment mechanisms; demand and recovery provisions; overview of GST 
accounting software; GST ledger creation, tax entries, return generation, and online GST portal 
operations.
unit4_text:
Module IV: Customs Duty Framework (8 Hours) 
Introduction to customs law; types of customs duties—basic, countervailing, safeguard, anti-dumping, 
and protective duties; valuation principles of imported and exported goods; import and export procedures; 
warehousing provisions; baggage rules and exemptions; duty drawback system; customs compliance 
provisions for concessional imports.

unit1_text:
Module I: Conceptual Framework of Investments (8 Hours) 
Meaning and nature of investment; investment objectives and process; investment vs speculation; risk and 
return concepts; investment avenues including equity, debt, mutual funds, commodities, and derivatives; 
role of investors and market participants in financial decision-making.
unit2_text:
Module II: Financial Markets and Instruments (10 Hours) 
Structure of financial markets; money market and capital market instruments; equity, debt, forex, 
commodity, and derivative markets; IPOs and exchange mechanisms; OTC vs exchange-traded markets; 
regulatory framework; role of RBI and SEBI in market regulation.
unit3_text:
Module III: Fundamental and Technical Analysis (10 Hours) 
Macroeconomic analysis (GDP, inflation, interest rates); industry and company analysis; financial 
statement interpretation; valuation basics; technical analysis concepts; charting techniques; Dow Theory; 
Elliott Wave Theory; chart patterns.
unit4_text:

Portfolio concept and diversification; Modern Portfolio Theory (Markowitz model); Efficient Frontier; 
CAPM framework; risk-return optimization; asset allocation strategies; active vs passive investment 
strategies; behavioural aspects of investing.
unit5_text:
Module V: Portfolio Performance Evaluation (6 Hours) 
Performance evaluation techniques; Sharpe Ratio, Treynor Ratio, Jensen’s Alpha; risk-adjusted return 
measures; portfolio revision and rebalancing; measurement of systematic and unsystematic risk; 
interpretation of portfolio outcomes; investor behaviour and decision biases.

unit1_text:
Module I: Financial System and Market Structure (10 Hours) 
Financial system: meaning, structure, functions, and significance; financial intermediation and role of 
intermediaries; money market instruments (Treasury Bills, CPs, CDs, call money, MMMFs); capital 
market structure; primary and secondary markets; IPOs, book building, rights issue, bonus issue; stock 
exchanges (NSE, BSE); trading mechanisms, settlement cycle (T+2), demat system; SEBI role and 
regulatory framework; investor protection mechanisms; Digital Financial Ecosystem in India (UPI, 
NEFT, IMPS architecture overview); Digital wallets and payment gateways; Introduction to Digital 
Banking and Neo-banks.
unit2_text:
Module II: Leasing and Hire Purchase (8 Hours) 
Concept of leasing; types of leases; lease evaluation from lessee and lessor perspectives; advantages and 
limitations; tax implications; buy vs lease decision-making; hire purchase system; comparison between 
hire purchase and installment purchase; major leasing institutions in India and their role in financial 
decision-making; Introduction to Blockchain and smart contracts in leasing agreements.
unit3_text:
Module III: Mutual Funds and Credit Rating (8 Hours) 
Mutual funds: structure, types, advantages, and limitations; NAV calculation; SIP and SWP; entry and 
exit loads; mutual fund regulation in India; credit rating agencies; rating process, symbols, and 
methodology; role and importance of credit ratings in investment decisions; Robo-advisory, Algorithm 
credits and AI-based portfolio recommendations
unit4_text:
Module IV: Securitisation and Financial Services (6 Hours) 
Concept of securitisation; process and structure; benefits and limitations; overview of financial services 
industry; fund-based vs fee-based services; role of financial intermediaries in service delivery; 
introduction to structured financial products in modern markets; Introduction to tokenisation of financial 
assets and RegTech (Regulatory Technology) for compliance automation.
unit5_text:
Module V: Factoring, Forfaiting and Bill Discounting (8 Hours) 
Factoring: meaning, types (recourse/non-recourse), domestic and international factoring; cost structure 
and process; bill discounting and rediscounting; forfaiting: mechanism, features, and applications; 
comparative analysis of factoring, forfaiting, and bill discounting; practical applications and numerical 
problems.

game, Assessment of EMH.

Investor Behaviour: Portrait of an individual investor, what the heuristics and biases mean for financial 
decision making, implications of: emotions and mental accounting. Behavioural portfolio theory, 
psychographic models, basic ingredients of sound investment philosophy, guidelines for overcoming 
psychological biases.
unit5_text:

Market outcomes: Size effect and seasonality, Momentum and reversal, post- earnings

Pricing Model. 
Value Investing: Central tenets of value investing, Evidence and prospects of value investing, 
Strategies of well-known value investors, academic research on value investing.

Global Financial Environment: Objective of financial management in a multinational

fisher effect.

transaction, transnational and economic exposure. Measurement of transaction exposure. 
Managing transaction exposure. Hedging Strategies.

framework. Benefits of inter-national equity and bond investing. International capital asset 
pricing model (ICAPM)

considerations in international capital budgeting. The adjusted present value approach (APV).

withholding tax. Foreign sales corporations, 80-20 subsidiaries and tax havens.

i) International cash management: The cash positioning decision. Advantages and disadvantages 
of centralized cash management. Multilateral netting. Intra corporate transfer of funds. 
Transfer pricing, problems of international cash management. 
ii) International Receivables management: Domestic v/s International receivables management. 
Letter of credit. International factoring and Accounts receivables. 
iii) International inventory management: Advance inventory purchases. Stockpiling.
unit5_text:
Unit -V (Session 08) 
International Financing Decisions: 
i) Euro-money and Eurobond Markets. Size of the Euro currency market. Growth of Euro Dollar 
market. Instruments and rate of Euro Currency Markets. Creation of Euro deposits. Syndicated 
Eurocurrency loan Market. International Bond Markets, Multi-currency bonds and their types. 
Rationale for multi currency bonds. 
ii)  International Equity markets: Foreign equity market and their comparative performance. 
Recent developments and innovations in international capital markets. Recent developments in 
the Euro bond market.

unit1_text:
UNIT I : Introduction                                                                                               (6 hours) 

Financial Credit: Meaning & Objectives, Credit Risk, Credit Analysis, Seven C’s, Credit Analysis 
Process, Credit Process, Documentation, Loan Pricing and Profitability Analysis. Regulations, 
Types of Credit Facilities: Various types of Credit Facilities- Cash Credit, Overdrafts, Demand 
Loan, Bill Finance – Drawee Bill Scheme, Bill Discounting. Cash Delivery: Types of Facilities, 
Modes of Delivery.
unit2_text:
UNIT II : Trade Credit Risk                                                                                   (8 hours) 
Sole -Banking Arrangement, Multiple Banking Arrangement, Consortium Lending, Syndication. 
Credit Thrust, Credit Priorities, Credit Acquisitions, Statutory & Regulatory restrictions on 
Advances. Credit Appraisal: Validation of proposal, Dimensions of Credit Appraisals, Structuring

Loan, Source of Repayment, Cash Flow, Collateral.

Quasi Credit Facilities: Advantages of Non-Fund Facilities, Various types of NFB Facilities, 
Various types Letter of Credits, Assessment of LC limits, Bills Purchase/ Discounting under LC, 
Loan commitments, Un-funded lines of credit and their characteristics 

Various types of Bank Guarantees: Performance Guarantee, Financial Guarantees, Deferred 
Payment Guarantees, Types of Performance and Financial Guarantees, Assessment of Bank 
Guarantees Limit, Period of Claim under Guarantee.
unit4_text:
UNIT IV : Operational Risk Overview                                                                 (08 hours) 
Risk & Uncertainty, Financial Sector, Risk Types, Operational Risk Management- Recruitment & 
Training, Work flow Design, Work Flow Documentation, Delegation of Authority, Independent 
Internal Audit, Independent Compliance Function, Independent Risk Management Function, 
System Audit, Corporate Governance, Whistle Blower Policy, Risk Management Culture.
unit5_text:
UNIT V : Credit Analysis & Rating                                                                       (08 hours) 
Importance of credit analysis, Stages of credit analysis profitability analysis and pricing of loans, 
Credit risk analysis (Debt ratios and risk of leverage), Analysis of working capital, liquidity, 
operating and cash cycle risk . 
Credit Rating: Measurement of Risk, Objective of Rating, Internal & External Rating, Model Credit 
Rating, Methodology of Rating, Internal & External Comparison, Model Rating Formats.

unit1_text:
Unit 1: Indian EXIM Framework and Registration 

                                      (8Hr) 
Latest Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) overview; objectives and key provisions; role of Directorate 
General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank), Export Promotion 
Councils (EPCs), Special Economic Zones (SEZs); types of exports and imports; registration 
processes including Import Export Code (IEC), Registration Cum Membership Certificate (RCMC) 
and Authorized Dealer Code (AD Code); overview of Start-up and Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises (MSME) support in India’s FTP.
unit2_text:
Unit 2: Commercial and Regulatory Documentation 

                                     (8Hr) 
Commercial documents: proforma invoice; commercial invoice; packing list; certificate of origin 
from Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) and chamber of commerce; inspection and 
quality certificates (Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), Agricultural and 
Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA); regulatory documents: 
shipping bill; bill of entry; Goods and Services Tax (GST) invoice for exports; e-invoicing 
compliance; overview of GST refund mechanisms for exports.
unit3_text:
Unit 3: Shipping, Logistics & Insurance Documentation                                                  (7Hr) 
Indian logistics infrastructure: Inland Container Depots (ICDs); Container Freight Stations 
(CFS); Special Economic Zones (SEZs); role of shipping lines and freight forwarders; types of 
shipments: Full Container Load (FCL) vs Less than Container Load (LCL); types of transport 
documents: bill of lading; airway bill; multimodal transport documents; marine insurance in India.
unit4_text:
Unit 4: Banking, Payment & Foreign Exchange Documents 
                                     (9Hr) 
Payment modes in Indian trade: advance payment; documents against payment (DP); documents 
against acceptance (DA); letter of credit (LC) process under Uniform Customs and Practice for 
Documentary Credits (UCPDC) norms; Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Foreign Exchange 
Management Act (FEMA) guidelines on foreign exchange (forex) management; Authorized Dealer 
(AD) bank’s role; banking documents: electronic Bank Realization Certificate (e-BRC); Foreign 
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC); Goods Receipt (GR) form; Shipping Declaration Form 
(SDF); steps for foreign currency realization and repatriation.
unit5_text:
Unit 5: Customs Procedures and Digital Trade Platforms 
                                        (8Hr) 
Overview of Indian Customs Act; customs clearance process for exports and imports; role of 
Customs House Agent (CHA); Indian Customs Electronic Gateway (ICEGATE) registration; 
uploading documents online (shipping bill, electronic Certificate of Origin (e-CoO), electronic 
Bank Realization Certificate (e-BRC)); Indian Single Window System; trade analytics and 
compliance monitoring tools.

Macro Economics, Managerial Economics and its relevance in business decisions. Fundamental Principles of 
Managerial Economics - Incremental Principle, Marginal Principle, Opportunity Cost Principle, Discounting 
Principle, Concept of Time Perspective, Equi-Marginal Principle, Utility Analysis, Cardinal Utility and Ordinal 
Utility. Case Studies
unit2_text:

Demand Function, Demand Schedule, Demand curve, Law of Demand, Exceptions to the law of Demand, 
Shifts in demand curve, Elasticity of Demand and its measurement. Price Elasticity, Income Elasticity, Arc 
Elasticity. Cross Elasticity and Advertising Elasticity. Uses of Elasticity of Demand for managerial decision 
making, Demand forecasting meaning, significance and methods. ( numerical Exercises) Case Studies 
Supply Analysis; Law of Supply, Supply Elasticity; Analysis and its uses for managerial decision making. 
Price of a Product under demand and supply forces . Case Studies
unit3_text:

function, Laws of production: Law of diminishing returns, Law of returns to scale. Cost concept and analysis: 
Cost, Types of costs, Cost output relationship in the short-run. Cost output relationship in the Long-run. 
Estimation of revenue. Average Revenue, Marginal Revenue. Case Studies
unit4_text:

determination of price under perfect competition. Monopoly: Feature, pricing under monopoly, Price 
Discrimination. Monopolistic: Features, pricing under monopolistic competition, product differentiation.

unit1_text:
Unit I (6 Hrs)-Operations Research & Decision-Making Environments
Operations Research:- Uses, Scope and Applications of Operation Research in managerial decision-
making .Decision-making environments:- Decision-making under certainty, uncertainty and risk situations;
Decision tree approach and its applications.
unit2_text:
Unit II (10 Hrs)-Linear Programming Problem & Transportation Problem
Linear programming: Mathematical formulations of LP Models for product-mix problems; graphical and
simplex method of solving LP problems; duality.
Transportation problem: Various methods of finding Initial basic feasible solution-North West Corner Method,
Least Cost Method & VAM Method and optimal solution-Stepping Stone & MODI Method, Maximization
Transportation Problem
unit3_text:
Unit III (8 Hrs)-Assignment model & Game Theory
Assignment model: Hungarian Algorithm and its applications, Maximization Assignment Problem.
Game Theory: Concept of game; Two-person zero-sum game; Pure and Mixed Strategy Games; Saddle Point;
Odds Method; Dominance Method and Graphical Method for solving Mixed Strategy Game.
unit4_text:
Unit IV (6 
Sessions)-Sequencing & Queuing Theory
Sequencing Problem:  Johnsons Algorithm for n Jobs and Two machines, n Jobs and Three Machines, Two jobs
and m - Machines Problems.
Queuing Theory:  Characteristics of M/M/I Queue model; Application of Poisson and Exponential distribution
in estimating arrival rate and service rate; Applications of Queue model for better service to the customers.
unit5_text:
Unit V (6 Hrs)-Replacement Problem & Project Management
Replacement Problem: Replacement of assets that deteriorate with time, replacement of assets which fail
suddenly.
Project Management:  Rules for drawing the network diagram, Applications of CPM and PERT techniques in
Project planning and control; crashing of operations.

impact of WTO on agribusiness.
co2_text:

agribusiness trade.
co3_text:
Apply key economic trade theories to evaluate India's position in 
global agribusiness trade.
co4_text:

unit1_text:
Unit I: Basics of International Trade and WTO (4 Hours) 
Introduction to international trade: concepts and importance; World Trade Organization (WTO): 
structure, functions, and role; Implications of WTO for Indian economy in general and agriculture in 
particular; Overview of global trade environment and challenges for agribusiness
unit2_text:
Unit II: WTO Agreements and Trade Regulations (6 Hours) 
Trade-Related Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS); Trade-Related Investment Measures (TRIMS); 
Quotas, anti-dumping duties, quantitative and qualitative restrictions; Tariff and non-tariff measures, 
trade liberalization; Subsidies, green box and red box measures under WTO; Future negotiation issues 
at WTO; Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) and carbon trading relevance to agribusiness 
sustainability.
unit3_text:
Unit III: Foreign Trade and Economic Theories (10 Hours) 
Importance of foreign trade for developing economies; Concepts of absolute and comparative 
advantage; Overview of India’s foreign trade with special focus on agriculture and agribusiness; 
Emerging trends and challenges in global agribusiness trade
unit4_text:
Unit IV: India’s Foreign Trade Policy and Economic Implications (10 Hours) 
Composition and features of India’s foreign trade policy; India’s balance of payments and its impact 
on trade; Inter-regional vs. international trade; Tariffs, trade controls, and exchange rate mechanisms; 
Foreign trade multiplier and its significance in economic growth; Foreign demand and supply side 
analysis in agribusiness trade; Opportunity cost and implications for developing countries; Trade and 
factor price relationships; Market entry methods for global agribusiness markets.
unit5_text:
Unit V: Export-Import Procedures and Market Entry (10 Hours) 

Export-import documentation and procedures: commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, 
certificate of origin, phytosanitary certificate, export/import license, letter of credit, insurance 
certificate, customs declaration, inspection certificate, consular invoice; Role of government and trade 
facilitation bodies; Logistics and supply chain management including cold chain and transportation; 
Marketing strategies for sustainable global agribusiness markets.

livestock production; Climate and weather risks: droughts, floods, storms, and weather aberrations; 
Asset risk: risks related to machinery, land, and infrastructure; Health risk: impact on farmers’ health 
and labor capacity

Effects of climate change and weather aberrations on crop yield; Socio-economic impacts on farming 
communities, with special focus on arid and semi-arid regions; Case studies highlighting regional 
vulnerabilities and adaptation challenges
unit4_text:

Risk identification and assessment techniques; Risk avoidance, reduction, and mitigation strategies; 
Role of diversification, improved agronomic practices, and technology adoption; Designing risk 
management products and programmes tailored for farmers

Overview of agricultural insurance schemes and products; Compensation mechanisms and claim 
processes; Legislative and regulatory framework supporting agricultural risk management; Estimation 
of losses and its importance in policy design; Role of government and private sectors in risk 
management and insurance

unit2_text:

project feasibility in various agribusiness sectors
unit3_text:

Preparation of project financial statements: projected income statement, balance sheet, cash flow 
statement; Sources of funds and capital structure for projects; Financial planning and budgeting for 
agribusiness projects; Case examples of project cost structuring
unit4_text:

Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR), Profitability Index;

evaluation; Social cost-benefit analysis and project sustainability; Case studies illustrating project 
appraisal in agribusiness

audit and feedback mechanisms; Managing project risks and mitigation strategies; Examples of 
successful and failed agribusiness projects with lessons learned

unit1_text:
Module I: Monetary Policy and Macroeconomic Environment Management (6 Hours) 
Monetary Policy and Macroeconomic Environment Management; Concept and Importance of Monetary Policy; 
Objectives of Monetary Policy: Price Stability, Employment Generation, Exchange Rate Stability, Balanced Economic 
Growth and Financial Stability. Conflict among Monetary Policy Objectives: Growth versus Inflation; Role of Monetary 
Policy in Economic Development; Inflation Management; Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism; Role of Central 
Bank in Macroeconomic Management. Case Studies: Monetary policy responses during inflationary pressures and 
economic slowdown.
unit2_text:
Module II: RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee and Monetary Policy Instruments (10 Hours) 
Formation of Monetary Policy Committee (MPC): Purpose, Functions, Constitution and Decision-Making Process; 
Instruments of Monetary Policy: Concept, Mechanism and Effectiveness of: Bank Rate, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), 
Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) Rate; Review of 
Monetary Policy Framework of the Reserve Bank of India during the last five years; Recent Monetary Policy Changes 
announced by RBI. Role of Central Banking in Emerging Economies; Digital Currency and Changing Role of Central 
Banks. Case Studies: RBI monetary policy decisions and their impact on inflation, growth and financial markets.
unit3_text:
Module III: Public Finance and Recent Macroeconomic Trends (8 Hours) 
Public Finance: Meaning, Scope and Importance; Role of Government in the Economy. Government Intervention: 
Public Goods, Externalities and Asymmetric Information. Fiscal Policy and Long-Term Economic Growth; Fiscal Policy 
and Equity; Fiscal Policy and Macroeconomic Stability. Interaction between Monetary Policy and Fiscal Policy; Fiscal-
Monetary Coordination. Recent Global and Regional Macroeconomic Trends; Impact of Global Economic Events on 
Domestic Policy Framework. Case Studies: Global financial crises, pandemic response, and economic recovery policies.
unit4_text:
Module IV: Fiscal Frameworks, Policies and Economic Impact (10 Hours) 
Fiscal Policy: Meaning, Objectives and Components. Government Expenditure in India: Capital Expenditure, Revenue 
Expenditure, Plan and Non-Plan Expenditure Fiscal Indicators: Fiscal Deficit, Primary Deficit,  Revenue Deficit; Impact 
of Fiscal Deficits on Economic Growth and Stability; Government Receipts: Capital Receipts, Revenue Receipts, Tax 
Revenue Non-Tax Revenue; Budget Estimates, Revised Estimates and Actual Estimates; Modern Budgeting Practices: 
Zero-Based Budgeting, Gender Budgeting; Fiscal Devolution and Centre-State Financial Relations; Role of Finance 
Commission; Case Studies: Union Budget analysis and fiscal policy reforms in India.
unit5_text:
Module V: Fiscal Policy Sustainability and Inclusive Growth (6 Hours) 
Fiscal Sustainability: Concept and Importance; Public Debt Management; Debt Tolerance and Fiscal Space. 
Fiscal Sustainability Analysis: Debt Projections,  Fiscal Risks,  Debt Sustainability Across Countries and Over Time 
Fiscal Space: Concept, Optimal and Safe Debt Levels; Relationship between Interest Rates and Public Debt. 
Fiscal Policy and Inclusive Growth: Poverty Reduction,  Employment Generation, Social Sector Development 
Sustainable Economic Growth; Case Studies: Sustainable fiscal practices and inclusive development strategies.
